title: Stock arrangements, requests and reading music in Celestin's band
summary: The band used stocks, he directed it, they never refused requests, bought hit stocks, and later played more from memory.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Did you use any arrangements other than stock arrangements?
No, that's all we used stock arrangements. Two stocks? It was very popular stock arrangements.
Did Celestan direct the saxophone section or would he let you work out?
No, I had all that to do. In fact, I used to direct the whole band. Different things we would play mostly my ideas. I was a very important man to Father Celestan.
Would they, if you were playing a dance, would they like to play requests? Did they play requests? Yeah, we played requests.
We used to like to play requests.
Did you ever turn down any requests? No, never did.

We never turned down a request. We loved their requests. Suppose you didn't know the number, what would you do about it? Well, we'd just tell them we don't know that number. But anything else they'd like to hear, they would play for them.
How often did you get new stocks in? I mean, say two or three people came up and asked for a number, would you go out and buy the stock or not? Which way would you do it?
We wouldn't go out and buy the stock unless it was popular. Unless it was a real hit.
But someone asked us for a number that's popular, we would go ahead and buy it.
That band was reading all the time. Did all this play for music, the Salisdain band?

Most of the playing was reading at that time. But later on we started playing a lot of music just from memory. Salisdain, well a few numbers Salisdain would play, and I would just get behind him. And I thought so he would play without music. But when I first got a man, Salisdain would play without music unless he played Home Sweet Home or Eliza Jane or something like that. Whoa, Nellie.
